title: LLV-GPP375: a single variable-output finish gives n^(15/4) classical space

claims.statement: For every N>=2 and s in Z/NZ, n=ceil(log2N), the single LLV-GPP375 configuration in proof.md recovers the entire secret with unconditional probability at least1-2^-8 from independent ideal copies. On EVERY branch its charged work is O(2^((1/2)sqrt nlog2n)), with an absolute outside constant and exact growth index1/2. The main branch n>=2^4096 computes v=floor(sqrt n),r=ceil(sqrt n),ell=ceil(log2n),a=floor(4v/7),H=bit_length(a^256-1),B_src=floor(v/2)-100ell-100,m=floor(256B_src/H),kappa=ceil(log2(m+2))+3,lambda=ceil((n+m*kappa)/(m*(a-1))). It uses full levels followed by ONE variable-arity/output finish k=ceil((R+kappa+1)/lambda), widthR and output log length1, including k=1,R=0. MERGEF handles f>=1, b>=0, variable mu and output length, with complete rank/phase, miss and conditional-incidence proofs. Literal Dbar=2K*lambda*a^(m+1),Dcap=2^12nDbar,Ccap=2^13nDbar, finite exhaustive branch and all-modulus decoders are specified. All source/extraction, serial lookup/list exclusion, addressing, generation, measurements, resets, discarded work and cleanup are charged. Section14 proves a negative93/8960sqrt n margin before lower-order polynomial work, yielding the exact pure upper envelope jointly with all other claims.

For the same LLV-GPP375 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, peak classical workspace is O(n^(15/4)) bits with an absolute outside constant and exact growth index0. Section8 proves2^lambda<=n^(7/4)/2. Section14 bounds O(n) retained tables, each O(n^(11/4)) bits; the single current tuple list uses O(n^(11/4)) bits, current input/sort/residue arrays O(n^(13/4)), and arithmetic, extraction and streamed decoder storage O(n^3) or less. Thus all classical components fit O(n^(15/4)), without a stored full tree or exponential circuit. This holds jointly with unconditional full-secret success and all other claims.

For this same LLV-GPP375 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, peak quantum allocation is O(n) qubits, with an absolute constant and exact growth index0. Full-level siblings use O(m*a*lambda), the single finish O(a*lambda), and each search uses fresh U=f*lambda and reusable O(U+b) scratch. Rank/projection, source and extraction registers are included and all trials reset/releases scratch. Section8 bounds the joint allocation by O(n), including failures and abort cleanup, jointly with full-secret success and all other claims.

For this same LLV-GPP375 configuration, every N,s and EVERY branch, fresh acquired source copies number O(2^((1/2)sqrt n)), with an absolute outside constant and exact growth index1/2. All failed, rejected, discarded and aborted copies are included. The literal main cap nCcap+K is at most2^((1/2)sqrt n), using Dbar=2K*lambda*a^(m+1),Dcap=2^12nDbar,Ccap=2^13nDbar and mH<=256B_src. One final variable-arity call gives height<=m+1 and expected leaf factor at most2lambda*a^(m+1); the exact source reserve covers the extra factor a. The finite branch changes only the outside constant. This is joint with unconditional full-secret success and every other resource/error claim.

For the same LLV-GPP375 algorithm and configuration of proof.md, the proved fractional error tolerance is epsilon(n) = 0: all Q source copies are independent ideal coset states. Under this promise, for every N and s, full-secret recovery succeeds with probability at least 1 - 2^-8 jointly with all four resource bounds. No positive corruption tolerance is asserted; this is not a proof that greater tolerance is impossible.

structured.error_model: Malformed fraction among acquired copies. The proved guarantee requires every copy to be an independent ideal coset state; no behavior is promised for malformed copies.
